changes.before: If the second queued value becomes 9, what is the drained total?
changes.after: Read the values that remain after a buffered channel closes.

before: make(chan int, 2) creates a channel with room for two queued integers. These two sends can complete without a receiver. Buffering does not make an unlimited queue or guarantee that another goroutine has finished processing a value.

Closing announces that no more values will be sent; it does not discard queued values. range drains the buffered values and stops after the closed channel is empty. Sending after close or closing twice panics; this example performs neither invalid operation.
Expected output or behavior: 7. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Use the two-result receive form to distinguish a valid zero from an empty closed channel. You may trace it without a Go compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A buffered channel has room for waiting values. `make(chan int, 2)` can hold two integers. Two sends fit here without a receiver. A full buffer makes further sends wait for space.

Closing tells receivers that no more values will be sent. It keeps queued items available. A range loop reads those items and stops once the closed channel is empty. Do not send after closing or close the same channel twice; either can panic.
The screen shows `7`. Closing preserves 3 and 4, and the loop adds both.
A two-result receive can also report whether an item was available. Its flag is false only after the closed channel is empty, so a real queued zero is still distinguishable.

after: Closing is different from clearing the queue.

before.question: If the second queued value becomes 9, what is the drained total?
choices: 0 because ranging a closed channel skips queued values.
3 because closing discards the buffered tail
before.explanation: Both queued integers remain available after close, so range sums three and nine.

after.question: Change the second queued value to 9. What total appears?
choices: 0, because a closed channel skips queued values.
3, because closing discards the last item.
after.explanation: Both values remain available after close. 3 plus 9 gives 12.
